chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Hariz, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

There is no owner of wealth of gold or silver who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will detain him on the Day of Judgment in a barren valley, and will send against him a hornless serpent who pursues him while he turns away from it; and when he sees that he cannot escape from it and it gains control over his hand, it bites him as one bites a date, until it becomes a collar around his neck.
And this is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'They shall have made to cleave to their necks that whereof they were niggardly' on the Day of Resurrection.

And there is no owner of wealth of camels or cows or sheep who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will detain him on the Day of Judgment in a barren valley, where every hoofed creature will tread on him with its hoof, and every toothed creature will gnaw at him with its tooth.

And there is no owner of wealth of date palms or vineyards or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will shackle him with the ring of his land until the seven earths, until the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.قَاعٍ قَرْقَرٍ: A barren, dry valley or desert

ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment in the afterlife for not paying Zakat on different types of wealth?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) details the specific eschatological retribution for withholding zakat, emphasizing that the punishment is tailored to the type of wealth withheld—whether gold, livestock, or produce—thereby illustrating the principle of *muqabala* (correspondence). This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the physical manifestation of stinginess as a literal shackle in the afterlife, reinforcing the Quranic promise that the withheld wealth itself becomes the instrument of torment.
